title: Working Parents Feel Torn: 'No Way to Be Two Things at Once'
summary: Have you ever felt like you're being pulled in two directions at once? That's how a lot of working parents feel every single day. A big new survey from Pew Research Center found that two out of three working moms say they can't give their all at home. More than half say the same about work. Dads feel it too—half say they can't give 100% at home, and about a third feel that way at work. Amber Petersen is a mom from Iowa who works at a law firm. She told NPR, 'I feel like that tug of war is constantly on my mind... There's just no way to be two things at once and give 100% at both.' Sometimes she has to leave work suddenly if one of her kids gets sick at school. But she doesn't get paid for those hours, which makes money tight. The survey talked to over 2,200 working parents. It found that more than half of parents with lower incomes worry about losing pay if they have to leave work for family stuff. Black and Hispanic parents worry about this more than white and Asian parents. Amber says paid sick leave would help a lot, and so would cheaper childcare. Last summer, she had to let her daughters stay home alone because a summer program cost thousands of dollars—way too much. Nearly half of working parents in the survey had trouble finding summer care. It's a tough juggling act, and parents are hoping for changes that make it a little easier.
why_it_matters: This might help you understand why your own parents sometimes seem stressed and why changes like cheaper camps or paid time off could make family life easier.

background_read: Pew Research Center is a group that studies how people live and think, sending surveys to thousands of families.
In the United States, many workers do not have paid sick leave, which means they get no money if they stay home to care for a sick child. Childcare can cost hundreds or thousands of dollars a month.
Black and Hispanic families often face more money challenges, which can make missing work even harder.
Article_Structure: WHO: Working moms and dads, Pew Research Center, Amber Petersen
WHAT: A big survey shows most working parents feel torn and can't give 100% at home or work
WHERE: Mostly in the United States, with Amber Petersen in Iowa
WHY: Parents lack paid leave and cheap childcare, making it hard to balance family and job

perspectives.description: They feel stretched thin and want more support from jobs and the government so they can take care of their kids without losing money.
Bosses might want workers to be available all the time, but not all companies offer paid sick leave or flexible hours.
Many people believe the government should help by making childcare cheaper and passing laws that give paid time off for families.
